name: Face pull
pattern: High pull to the face with external rotation: elbows pull out and back at shoulder height, then the hands turn back beside the ears.
setup: Set a rope at about eye height; hold the ends with thumbs pointing back toward you.
Step back until the arms are straight and the weight is off the stack.
Stand tall, feet hip width or staggered, ribs down.

steps.text: Arms straight forward at shoulder height, shoulder blades slightly spread.
Pull the rope toward your face, elbows high and wide, shoulder blades squeezing back.
Finish by turning your hands back so they end beside your ears, knuckles up, like a double biceps pose.
Reverse the path slowly until your arms are straight.

cues.cue: Elbows at shoulder height, pointing out to the sides.
cues.why: Pulling with the arms out at the side and turning out is the position where the rear delt and middle trapezius are most active.

cues.cue: Finish with your hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
cues.why: Adding external rotation at the end works the infraspinatus and lower trapezius; palms-up pulls raised both.

cues.cue: Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, not up.
cues.why: Exercises with low upper-trap to mid and lower trap ratios are preferred for scapular balance.

cues.cue: Stand tall; do not lean back to finish the rep.
cues.why: Leaning turns it into a row and uses the body weight instead of the rear shoulder.

cues.cue: Use a light weight you can hold at the end for one second.
cues.why: Face pulls give rear-delt force similar to a bent-over rear raise, so heavy loads are not needed.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.

tempo.note: Pull in 1 second, hold the end 1 second, return in 2.

mistakes.name: Elbows drop
mistakes.looks: The elbows fall to the ribs and the rope comes to the chest, like a row.
mistakes.fix: Raise the anchor and keep the elbows level with the shoulders.
mistakes.why: With the elbows low the lats and biceps take over and the rear shoulder works less.

mistakes.name: No turn-out at the end
mistakes.looks: The hands stop in front of the face, forearms pointing forward.
mistakes.fix: Pull the ends apart and turn your hands back beside your ears.
mistakes.why: Skipping the rotation misses most of the rotator cuff work.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears as the rope comes in.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; shoulders down first, then pull.
mistakes.why: The upper trapezius takes over from the middle and lower trapezius.

safety: Shoulder pain at the end: stop the rotation short and keep the elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Use a rope or band so the hands can move apart freely.

variants.change: Palms up grip: more infraspinatus and lower trapezius.
Seated or kneeling: less trunk lean available, stricter.
One arm: trunk resists twisting; same arm path.
Lying face up under the cable: the back is supported, same arm path.
Body-weight version leaning back on straps: harder as the feet move forward.
Bent over with dumbbells: trunk near horizontal, elbows pull out and up, then turn out.

metrics.label: Elbow height
metrics.good: 75-95 at the end (elbows at shoulder level)

motion.basis: End position matches the prone horizontal abduction with external rotation tested in reinold2004 and ekstrom2003; hand position effect from fukunaga2022 (band pull-apart). Scapular upward rotation near 20° at 85° abduction from ludewig2009 rhythm, estimated. Few studies test the face pull itself (zhu2025, model-based), so joint angles are mainly coaching convention.
